verdict: Nike's revenue fell 4% to $11.2B as Greater China dropped 22% and Converse shrank by more than a quarter, but tighter costs under the new 'Pace' program kept net profit nearly flat at $712M — and gross margin actually improved.

segments.name: North America
segments.note: Nike's home market — the only region that grew, on footwear +1% and apparel +6%.

segments.name: Europe, Middle East & Africa
segments.note: Footwear fell 11%, partly offset by apparel growth of 5%.

segments.name: Asia Pacific & Latin America
segments.note: Roughly flat once currency moves are stripped out.

segments.name: Greater China
segments.note: The problem spot — footwear fell 22% as Nike repositions the brand and works through excess stock.

segments.name: Converse
segments.note: The Chuck Taylor brand — down 28%, with declines in every territory.

segments.name: Global Brand & Corporate
segments.note: Licensing and other brand-division revenue, net of a small corporate revenue adjustment.

opex.name: Demand creation
opex.note: Advertising and sports marketing — up 5% as Nike spent behind major sports events.

opex.name: Operating overhead
opex.note: Salaries, technology and running the business — down 6% on cost discipline under the Pace program.

takeaways.title: North America is stabilizing
takeaways.text: Home-market revenue rose 2% to $5.1B — the only region in growth — and wholesale overall fell just 1%, suggesting the product reset is landing with retailers.

takeaways.title: Greater China is the drag
takeaways.text: China revenue fell 22% (26% before currency) and Converse dropped 28%. Nike says it is repositioning both brands rather than discounting its way out.

takeaways.title: Pace: the big cost program
takeaways.text: Nike's new transformation program targets about $2.5B of savings through fiscal 2031, at roughly $1.0B of charges along the way. Overhead already fell 6% this quarter.

otherDetail: Other income of $33M, net — $14M of net interest income plus $19M of other income.
oneTimers: Nike's 'Pace' transformation brings severance and employee-related charges — about $0.3B expected in fiscal 2027 (roughly $0.15 per share) — that sit inside its normal cost lines rather than on a separate line. Nike's adjusted EPS leaves them out; the GAAP diluted EPS here is $0.48.
